title: A runner's ready mark always arms a wake, and each wake line names the minutes a green PR has sat unmerged (runners 10, 11 and 12)
why: Debt named by runner 10 (09:07 CST Nov 14, relayed), widened by the consultant's 09:07 ask via the coordinator (09:09, relayed; triage read none of it). Two gaps, not one: (1) #2942 green about 16 min unmerged (05:41 to 06:03 CST; runner 10 reported its own session idle then, a gap in its own turns); (2) #3238 (no wake from 08:30 to 09:04; ready run 43604213305 green 08:48:39, merged 09:06:14: 17 min). Runner 10 said at 06:07 it would hold a PR subscription at each ready mark, and the second gap happened anyway (n=2, one runner). Fix shape asked by the consultant: (a) a ready mark always arms a wake, either a PR subscription or a one-time check-in at the run's expected end; (b) each wake line names the minutes a green PR has sat unmerged; (c) scope: runners 10, 11 and 12. Reads: runner 11 named a check-in at each ready mark tonight (#704 ready 07:57, #710 ready 08:40, "check-in in 15 min"); runner 12 unread. The coordinator asked runner 10 why (subscription not set, or set and no wake) and runner 12 the same, and passes the answers. Earlier rescope (coordinator 09:08): root rule git-ci-wait-checks-in already says a session that waits on CI sets a one-time check-in when it starts to wait, so a first fix is a handoff line, not a tool. The consultant's shape adds the second half: the wake line carries the sat-minutes. Whether a tool must arm it, or a handoff line suffices, waits for the answers on why runner 10's subscription did not wake it; if "set and no wake", the cause is in the wake path (a tool or harness fault), not in the runner. Done when: the cause of both gaps is named, runners 10, 11 and 12 each carry the rule, and no green ready run waits over 10 min across the next 5 merges per runner (a count from the merge log; unmeasured now). Folded here, no second record (consultant 09:07). CAUSE NAMED 09:21 CST Nov 14 (runner 10's own answer, 09:08, via the coordinator 09:10; relayed): runner 10 set NO check-in at the ready marks of #3397 (08:28) and #3389 (09:05); its first is at 09:06, firing 09:22 CST; "both gaps are mine"; from now one check-in at each ready mark, named with its time in its line. So both gaps are a runner rule not followed, not a wake-path fault: the earlier question "subscription set, or set and no wake" is answered for runner 10 (not set). Runner 12 unread. Remaining: the handoff line for runners 10, 11 and 12, and the count over the next 5 merges per runner. Tool change only if the miss recurs after the line. RUNNER 12 09:23 CST Nov 14 (its 09:09 message via the coordinator 09:11; self-reported from run records and its own check-ins; triage read none): it arms a one-time check-in (send_later) at a GUESSED end of the run; no PR subscription; no wake tied to the run ending. Green and unmerged over 10 min tonight: mailaudit #324 39 min (green 04:17, merged 04:56 CST), q_max #1174 20 min (green 05:50, read 06:10), mailaudit #328 22 min (green 01:57, merged 02:19). Under 10 min: q_max #1173 5 min, mailaudit #329 about 9 min. Runner 10: two gaps (16 and 17 min), no check-in set at two ready marks. Runner 11: names a check-in at each ready mark, no gap read. Fix shape (coordinator, to fold): arm the wake at the run's end event, not a guessed delay: a PR subscription (subscribe_pr_activity) at each ready mark. Whether runner sessions can subscribe, and whether a subscription wakes on a GREEN run, are not tested by the coordinator or triage (the root rules say a run with a red job sends no "all checks done" wake and a red run posts one PR comment). Runner 12 queued step ci-wait-wakes-on-run-end: same step, one record (the name is not used). HOME OF THE FIX: step ci-wait-subscribes-first (doing, runner 10's lane: a hook on the ready mark warns when the session has not called subscribe_pr_activity for that PR; rule git-ci-wait-checks-in names the subscription first); this step carries the samples and the done count. TEST READ 09:27 CST Nov 14 (runner 10's own account via the coordinator 09:12; unread by the coordinator and triage): subscribe_pr_activity has worked for runner 10 all night (wakes for #3395, #3238, #3389, #3272), so sessions can subscribe. A green wake DID arrive for a draft-era run: #3238 draft run ended green 14:18:49Z, wake (check_suite.completed) queued 14:18:58Z, 9 s (n=1). For #3238's READY run (green 14:48:39Z = 08:48 CST) it read no wake, but its session was idle 08:30 to 09:04, so a lost wake is not ruled out; unmeasured. Runner 10 runs the clean test at its next ready marks (#3401 first, #3397 after): subscribe plus one-time check-in plus REST updated_at against wake arrival; the coordinator passes the result. Status: sessions can subscribe (read); green wakes exist on at least draft runs (n=1); a ready-run green wake is unproven.
note: Filed 09:14 CST Nov 14 by triage. Tracker: the coordinator. No lane yet.
